answer: One concrete Sybil brake is a bonded entry stake that must survive a slow vesting window. Each agent locks a deposit before transacting, and trust is extended only after that bond matures. Faking a thousand identities is cheap; funding a thousand deposits and waiting out every vesting period is not, so attacker cost grows with each phantom while an honest agent pays once. A shared reputation map exposes clones: a newcomer claiming a crowded haven of vouches traces to one small garden of wallets funded from a single source. Like a cedar grown from seed, real trust needs time.
